name: GenFall
description: Reliable wearable fall detection requires large-scale and diverse datasets of falls and activities of daily living, yet collecting real-world falls from the elderly is ethically and practically challenging. We propose GenFall, a configurable synthetic fall dataset generated via diffusion-based text-to-motion models trained on large-scale human motion corpora. Virtual inertial signals, comprising triaxial accelerometer/gyroscope data, are computed from generated 3D trajectories to emulate sensors at arbitrary body positions. Each motion sequence undergoes rigorous quality control to ensure biomechanical plausibility and temporal continuity, resulting in a physically consistent dataset. Using GenFall, we evaluate the influence of dataset scale on fall-detection performance through representative neural architectures, including an LSTM baseline and a CNN–LSTM hybrid. Results demonstrate that training with larger-scale synthetic data improves model robustness and generalization, with the CNN–LSTM structure capturing superior spatiotemporal patterns. GenFall provides a scalable foundation for developing and benchmarking wearable fall-detection algorithms based on generative data.
